title: Looking for anyone to give a brief breakdown on how they have been implementing AI Tools
poster_role: Legal practitioner; exact role not stated
task_tested: Triage and first-pass review of routine agreements and subpoenas, batch document synthesis, and first drafts of legal work product; legal research was performed separately
reported_outcome: A practitioner reported that Claude was promising for triaging routine agreements and subpoenas and was very effective for synthesizing batches of documents and preparing first drafts after the practitioner supplied the facts and law. They said Claude was not a research service and that they verified its work.
chatgpt_or_claude_comparison: Claude was compared with the firm’s paid legal stack: LexisNexis and PACER remained the practitioner’s research sources, while Claude was used for document-heavy workflow and drafting support.
evidence_excerpt: It has been truly great for augmentation purposes like synthesizing batches of documents and doing first drafts of work product once I have worked through the underlying facts and law with it. As others point out it isn’t a research service.
notes: Direct practitioner report in a lawyer-centred community. Reddit JSON verified the URL and creation date as 2026-06-12; exact URL was checked against all existing raw JSONL files and was not found.
